title: Is Polk Audio Good? Our Verdict on Every Polk Speaker Line
metaDescription: Yes, Polk Audio is good, especially Signature Elite: the ES20 scores 84/100 vs a 78.8 bookshelf average. Where Polk is great value and where it falls short.
intro:
**Yes, Polk Audio is a good speaker brand**, and its mid-range Signature Elite line is one of the better values in home theater. Across the 16 Polk products in our database, the Signature Elite ES20 bookshelf scores **84/100** against an average of 78.8 for the 13 bookshelf speakers we track, and the ES60 tower **83** against a tower average of 80. The budget Monitor XT line is fine for a first system, while Polk's older PSW10 subwoofer is the weak spot.

This verdict is built from spec sheets and our research scores, not from hands-on listening. It covers who Polk is, which lines are worth buying, where Polk falls short, and how it compares with Klipsch. For the full lineup ranked, see our [Polk speaker review](/polk-audio-review/).
quickAnswer: **Yes.** Polk is a well-established US brand (founded in Baltimore in 1972) whose **Signature Elite** speakers score above our category averages and whose **Monitor XT** speakers are solid budget picks. Buy Signature Elite for a mid-price 5.1 or Atmos system; skip the PSW10 sub and expect Signature Elite to need more amplifier power than horn-loaded Klipsch speakers.

picks.body: The ES20 is the strongest case for Polk: **84/100**, the highest bookshelf score in Polk's range and above the 78.8 average across our 13 bookshelf speakers. It suits fronts in a small room or surrounds behind ES60 towers. The trade-off is efficiency: at 86 dB sensitivity it needs about seven times the power of the 94.5 dB [Klipsch RP-600M II](/gear/klipsch-rp-600m-ii/) to play equally loud, so pair it with a receiver that has some headroom.

The ES60 scores **83/100**, above the 80 average of the ten towers we track, and anchors a matched Signature Elite system with the [ES35 center](/gear/polk-signature-elite-es35/) (82). It is the tower to buy if you want a smooth, non-fatiguing sound for films and music. Like the ES20, it is less efficient than horn-loaded rivals and has a large footprint.

Polk's soundbar system comes with its own wireless sub and rear speakers and scores **82/100**, above the 80.4 average of the 12 soundbars we track. It is the Polk to buy if you want bar, sub and real rears in one box. Its app is less polished than Sonos's, and the full system takes more space than a single bar.

The Monitor XT20 scores **77/100**, just under the bookshelf average, at a much lower price band ($150–$250 a pair). It is a sound first-system or surround speaker. Expect a vinyl-wrapped cabinet and treble that is less refined than Signature Elite.

The pattern is clear: **Signature Elite and Polk's in-wall speakers beat the category average; Monitor XT sits near it; the budget subwoofers sit below it.** Scores are research scores from spec sheets, room maths and owner reports; see [how we score](/how-we-test/).

sections.heading: Who makes Polk Audio?
sections.body: Polk Audio was founded in Baltimore in 1972. It became part of Sound United, alongside Denon and Marantz, and Sound United was bought by Masimo in 2022. In 2025 Masimo agreed to sell Sound United, including Polk, to Harman, which is owned by Samsung. Polk still sells the same main lines: Monitor XT (budget), Signature Elite (mid-range) and Reserve and Legend (premium).

sections.heading: What does Polk do well?
sections.body:
- **Matched families.** Each line has towers, bookshelves, a center, height modules and subwoofers, so a 5.1.2 system sounds consistent from front to back.
- **Value in the middle.** Signature Elite scores above average at mid-range price bands.
- **Atmos options at low prices.** The [Monitor XT90](/gear/polk-monitor-xt90/) Atmos module costs $130–$200 a pair.
- **Wide availability.** Polk is sold at most big US retailers and on Amazon, so parts of a system are easy to add later.

sections.heading: Where does Polk fall short?
sections.body:
- **Efficiency.** Signature Elite speakers need more power than horn-loaded Klipsch models to play as loud; budget receivers can run out of headroom in big rooms.
- **Budget subwoofers.** The PSW10 (64) and Monitor XT12 (73) have 50 W RMS amps that limit output. Spend on the [Signature Elite ES12](/gear/polk-signature-elite-es12/) or a sub from our [best budget subwoofer](/best-budget-subwoofer-for-home-theater/) list instead.
- **Budget finishes.** Monitor XT cabinets are vinyl-wrapped.

sections.heading: Is Polk better than Klipsch?
sections.body: It depends on your receiver and taste. Klipsch's horn-loaded tweeters are more efficient, so they play louder on a small receiver and sound more forward. Polk's Signature Elite sounds smoother and less bright but needs more power. In our scores, Klipsch averages 80.0 across 19 products and Polk 77.6 across 16; Polk's average is pulled down by its budget subs, while its Signature Elite speakers match or beat comparable Klipsch models. See the [Klipsch home theater review](/klipsch-home-theater-review/).

mistakes.title: Pairing Signature Elite with an underpowered receiver
mistakes.body: At 86 dB sensitivity, the ES20 needs real power. Check your receiver's rated watts at 8 ohms, two channels driven.

mistakes.title: Saving money on the subwoofer
mistakes.body: Polk's cheapest subs score lowest in its range. A better sub matters more than a better tweeter.

mistakes.title: Mixing Polk lines across the front stage
mistakes.body: Keep the front left, center and right from the same series so voices pan smoothly.

faqs.q: Is Polk Audio a good brand?
faqs.a: Yes. Its Signature Elite speakers score above our category averages, and its Monitor XT speakers are solid budget picks. The weak spot is its cheapest subwoofers.
Neither wins outright. Klipsch is more efficient and sounds more forward; Polk Signature Elite is smoother but needs more power. Match the brand to your receiver and taste.
Polk is a US brand founded in Baltimore. Like most speaker brands at these prices, its speakers are manufactured overseas; check the box or listing for the country of origin.
Polk is part of Sound United, which Masimo bought in 2022. In 2025 Masimo agreed to sell Sound United to Harman, a Samsung subsidiary.

faqs.q: Are Polk Monitor XT speakers good?
faqs.a: For the price, yes. The XT20 and XT60 score 77/100, close to category averages, at budget price bands. Signature Elite is the step up.

faqs.q: Is the Polk PSW10 subwoofer good?
faqs.a: It is the weakest Polk product we track (64/100): a 10-inch driver and 50 W RMS amp limit output. It suits small rooms or older stereo systems only.

bottomLine: Polk Audio is good, and **Signature Elite is the line to buy**: the [ES20](/gear/polk-signature-elite-es20/), [ES60](/gear/polk-signature-elite-es60/) and [ES35](/gear/polk-signature-elite-es35/) all score above our category averages. Monitor XT is a fair budget choice; skip the PSW10. Give Signature Elite a receiver with headroom. See the full lineup in the [Polk speaker review](/polk-audio-review/) and compare with the [best bookshelf](/best-bookshelf-speakers-for-home-theater/) and [best tower speakers](/best-tower-speakers-for-home-theater/).
